title: Vendor Operations Manager - Global Support Operations
description:
**About the Role**  
  
Uber’s Global Support Organization (GSO) partners with Community Operations to deliver exceptional customer experiences across Mobility, Delivery, Global Programs, and Platform Integrity. We drive growth and satisfaction by optimizing Business Process Outsource (BPO) strategy, scaling efficient processes, and building strong vendor partnerships across markets and languages.  
  
As a **Vendor Manager**, you will support vendor performance and operational execution across one or more BPO/ Contact center partners, ensuring alignment with Global Support Operations (GSO) and Customer Advocacy and Solutions (CAS) priorities.GSO is part of the CAS organisation. Working in a matrixed environment, you will collaborate with cross-functional teams to monitor performance, address operational issues, and drive improvements within your assigned scope.  
  
In this role, you will manage day-to-day vendor interactions, track performance across quality, efficiency, productivity, and customer outcomes, and help implement established governance and performance frameworks. You will identify and escalate operational risks, and support resolution plans, support improvement initiatives, and contribute to maintaining strong partner relationships.  
  
We’re looking for a detail oriented and proactive professional who thrives in dynamic environments, manages priorities effectively, and communicates clearly to support alignment and consistent execution.  
  
**This role requires an overlap with US working hours between 8 AM Eastern Standard Time to 6 PM Eastern Standard time.**  
  
**Basic Role Qualifications**  

* **Experience:** 5+ years in Customer Experience, Support Operations, Program Management, Vendor Management (not supply management or procurement), or BPO/in-house contact center operations, with exposure to large-scale global support environments. Possess deep understanding of all CX KPIs and have a customer obsession.
* **Education:** Bachelor’s degree in a related field or equivalent experience
* **Project Management:** Demonstrated ability to lead projects, support team coordination, and share knowledge and support teammates where needed; prior direct people management experience is a plus.
* **BPO Operations:** Experience working with outsourced customer support operations, including performance tracking, vendor coordination, or operational support activities.
* **Stakeholder Management:** Ability to collaborate effectively with internal teams and vendor partners to support operational goals within defined responsibilities.
* **Analytical & Problem Solving:** Solid analytical skills, with the ability to interpret operational data and support recommendations for performance improvements.
* **Communication:** Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to work effectively with operational teams and partners.
* **Technical Fluency:** Proficient in Google Workspace and familiar with modern productivity or analytics tools including deep expertise in various AI tools specifically in using Gemini.
* **Language:** Professional fluency in English required; fluency in Hindi/ other local languages is a strong plus.
* **Travel:** Willingness to travel domestically and internationally 25%-50% of the time.

  
**What We Need from You**  

* **Execution Focus:** Comfortable working in the details, solving problems, and supporting operational improvements.
* **Comfort with Ambiguity:** Able to prioritize tasks and adapt in a fast-changing environment with minimal supervision. Acting always as an owner who takes charge and solves problems.
* **Collaborative Approach:** Builds positive working relationships and partners effectively with stakeholders and vendors.
* **Customer Focus:** Demonstrates commitment to operational quality and improving the support experience.

  
**Bonus Points if**  

* Experience in Tech, Mobility (Transport), Food, or Retail Delivery industries.
* Experience supporting process improvement or operational excellence initiatives.
* Experience with basic SQL
* Lean Six Sigma, PMP, COPC, or Change Management certification.

  
**Ready to Ride?**  
  
This isn't the kind of place where you follow a playbook — it's where you help write one. If you're driven by impact, energized by challenge, and ready to shape how the world moves — we'd love to hear from you.  
  
You may be eligible for bonuses, equity, and other compensation, as well as a range of benefits. Explore our benefits.  
  
Offices remain key to collaboration and Uber's culture. Unless approved for full remote work, employees must spend at least 50% of their time in-office. Some roles, like those at greenlight hubs, require full-time in-office presence. Ask your Recruiter for details about this role's requirements.  
  
Uber is proud to be an Equal Opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, race, color, religion, national origin, disability, protected Veteran status, age, or any other characteristic protected by law. We also consider qualified applicants regardless of criminal histories, consistent with legal requirements. If you have a disability or special need that requires accommodation, please let us know by completing this form.

title: Project & Creative Operations Lead
description:
**About TripleDart**
--------------------

TripleDart Digital is an AI-native, full-funnel growth agency built for B2B SaaS. We run paid media, ABM, SEO/GEO, creative, web/CRO and RevOps for 100+ SaaS brands scaling from $5M to $100M+ ARR across the US, Europe and APAC. Clients measure us on qualified pipeline and revenue influenced, and we hold Google Premier, HubSpot Platinum and LinkedIn Corporate Partner status.

Our paid media and ABM programs generate a steady stream of creative work — ad concepts, static and video assets, landing pages, ABM personalization, reporting dashboards. Delivering that at scale, to a US client's expectations, is an operations problem. This role owns it.

**Role Summary**
----------------

You are accountable for the entire paid media and creative operations layer: intake, scoping, scheduling, capacity, SLAs, QC and delivery across the portfolio. Account managers own the client relationship and strategy; you own that what we committed gets built correctly and ships on time.

This is a run-the-system-and-make-it-better role. You've managed delivery at scale before, you know what a healthy ClickUp board looks like, and you don't wait for a miss to find out a process is broken.

**What you'll own**
-------------------

### **Project management across the portfolio**

* Own intake to delivery for every paid media, ABM and creative request across ~15 accounts: scoping, briefs, estimates, scheduling, dependencies and sign-off.
* Run the weekly delivery rhythm — sprint planning, daily stand-ups with pods and creative, and a Friday portfolio review of what shipped, what slipped and why.
* Maintain a single, current view of every account's open work, due dates and blockers that an account manager or founder can read in 30 seconds.

### **SLAs and quality control**

* Define and enforce SLAs by deliverable type (ad copy, statics, video, landing pages, dashboards, campaign builds) and report adherence weekly.
* Build and run the QC layer: checklists, review gates and sign-off before anything reaches a client. Brand, copy, spec, tracking and link checks are non-negotiable.
* Track rework and client-reported misses as a defect rate, root-cause them and close the loop with the function that caused them.

### **Creative operations**

* Own the creative pipeline end to end: briefing standards, asset specs per channel (Google, LinkedIn, Meta, Reddit, CTV), versioning, approvals and asset handoff to paid media.
* Balance load across copy, design, video and web/dev; forecast creative demand from the media plan and staff or reprioritise ahead of the crunch.
* Maintain the creative library, naming conventions and templates so nothing ships off-brand or off-spec.

### **Capacity planning and ClickUp hygiene**

* ClickUp is the source of truth and you keep it that way: every task scoped, owned, estimated, dated and in the right status. No work outside the system.
* Run capacity planning per pod and per function against the retainer scope; flag over-servicing and under-utilisation to leadership monthly.
* Own time-tracking discipline and the utilisation and SLA dashboards leadership uses to run the BU.

### **Client communication**

* Be the delivery voice on client accounts alongside the account manager: status updates, timelines, revision rounds and expectation-setting on what ships when.
* Handle client-facing delivery escalations directly and proactively — before the client raises them.

### **Cross-functional problem solving**

* Sit between account management, paid media pods, copy, design, dev and analytics. When something is stuck, you unblock it, and you fix the process so it doesn't stick again.
* Document and improve SOPs for recurring work; bring AI and automation (ClickUp automations, n8n, Claude) into intake, QC and reporting to cut manual effort.

**How success is measured**
---------------------------

Delivery is under control when the client never has to ask where something is.

KPI

Target

What it measures

  

On-time delivery

95%+ of deliverables shipped by committed date

Scheduling and dependency control across the portfolio

  

SLA adherence

95%+ by deliverable type, reported weekly

Turnaround commitments kept per account

  

QC pass rate

98%+ first-pass; zero client-reported brand, spec or tracking errors

Quality gates working before work reaches the client

  

Rework rate

Under 10% of creative deliverables needing a second revision round

Briefing quality and QC discipline

  

ClickUp hygiene

100% of active work scoped, owned, estimated and dated; weekly audit score

The system reflects reality

  

Capacity utilisation

Pods and creative functions within 90–95% planned utilisation; over-servicing flagged monthly

Retainer scope matched to effort

  

Client delivery satisfaction

4.5+ / 5 on delivery and communication in QBR feedback

Clients trust the process, not just the people

  

Process improvement

At least one SOP or automation shipped per month with measured time saved

The system gets better, not just maintained

Targets are reviewed quarterly with the Head of Paid Media and feed the BU's business review.

**Who you are**
---------------

### **Non-negotiables**

* 5–8 years in project, delivery or operations management, with at least 3 years running delivery at scale — 10+ concurrent client accounts or 50+ live deliverables a month — at a marketing agency, creative studio or SaaS marketing team.
* A recognized PM certification: PMP, PRINCE2, CAPM, CSM/PSM or equivalent. Google Project Management or ClickUp certifications are a plus on top, not a substitute.
* Expert in ClickUp or an equivalent (Asana, Monday, Jira) — you've designed the workspace, the custom fields, the automations and the dashboards, not just used them.
* Hands-on experience running creative operations: briefing, asset specs across paid channels, review and approval cycles, and managing designers, copywriters and video editors' load.
* Working knowledge of paid media and ABM delivery — what a campaign build, a landing page or a reporting dashboard needs before it can ship — enough to QC it and estimate it.
* Accountability as a reflex. You have owned delivery outcomes personally, carried the miss, and fixed the process after.
* Clear, direct written and spoken English; you write client status updates and run calls with US stakeholders.
* Comfortable with US-overlap hours (2:00–11:00 PM IST) and a fully remote, cross-functional team.

### **Strong plusses**

* Six Sigma, Lean or ITIL exposure; you think in defect rates and cycle times.
* Experience with capacity planning and utilisation reporting against retainer scopes.
* Familiarity with Figma, Google Ads, LinkedIn Campaign Manager, GA4 and Looker Studio.
* Experience building ClickUp or n8n automations, or using Claude/ChatGPT to speed up intake, QC and reporting.
* Prior ownership of SOP libraries, onboarding playbooks or delivery handbooks.

### **How you work**

You are organized to the point of being predictable, and the team relies on that. You communicate early, especially bad news. You solve the problem in front of you and then remove the cause. You hold a standard without needing to be the loudest person on the call.

**Why join us**
---------------

* **Own the whole system.** Paid media and creative operations across the portfolio report into you — not a slice of one account.
* **Scale that matters.** 15 accounts, six delivery pods and a creative team shipping for US SaaS brands scaling to $100M+ ARR.
* **Build with AI.** We use Claude, n8n and ClickUp automations in delivery today; you'll have the mandate and budget to push that further.
* **A direct line to leadership.** You report to the Co-Founder running the BU; your dashboards are the ones the business is run on.
* **A clear path.** This role grows into Head of Delivery / Operations as the BU scales.

**Working setup and benefits**
------------------------------

* Fully remote. Work from anywhere in India.
* Fixed US-overlap shift: 2:00–11:00 PM IST, Monday to Friday, so you cover the India afternoon handoff and the full US morning.
* Learning and development budget — PM and platform certifications, courses and conferences.
* Full access to TripleDart's AI-native tooling stack (Claude, ChatGPT, ClickUp, n8n and internal platforms).
* Health insurance and wellbeing support [confirm plan details with HR].

**How to apply**
----------------

**Apply through Keka, or email your resume and cover letter to mailto:sabari@tripledart.com.**

**About the Delivery Amplification Office:**

The Delivery Amplification Office (DAO) is not a traditional PMO. We are an AI-native delivery function that makes engineering faster, clearer and easier to steer.

We run on the following two foundations.

**Amplified Squads** is our AI-native operating model. Small, goal-aligned squads with AI built into how they plan, track, report and ship. Agents and automation handle intake, hygiene and status, so people spend their time on decisions and delivery.

Our **Delivery Intelligence Platform** is the centre of everything we do. It is an always-on layer across Jira, Confluence, Slack and our people systems that turns delivery activity into live signal: squad health, risk, throughput, release status and executive briefs. Every squad, epic, release and report flows through it — and Delivery Operations keeps it true.

**What You'll Do:**

The Senior Delivery Operations Manager owns the operating system of one or more Business Lines (BLs): the data, cadence, tooling and automation that Amplified Squads run on. Paired with a Senior Delivery Lead as daily working partner and growth-path mentor, you move from keeping the system accurate to redesigning it — on a deliberate path toward Delivery Lead.

* **Operating Model Stewardship**
  + Own Amplified Squads health for 1–2 BLs: lifecycle adherence, goal coverage, squad lifespan and dissolution postponements.
  + Set and enforce operating conventions (naming, release versions, mandatory fields, dissolution checks), and document them in the DAO playbook.
  + Turn squad retrospectives and survey data into concrete changes to how squads form, run and close.

* **Delivery Intelligence Platform Ownership**
  + Act as the operations voice of the platform: define business logic, data-quality rules and acceptance criteria, and run UAT with the Delivery Engineers who build it.
  + Drive adoption so squads, EMs and PMs work from the platform, not from side spreadsheets.
  + Turn its signals into early warnings that reach your Delivery Lead before a review does.

* **Automation and AI Agents**
  + Maintain the ops automation backlog for your BLs: every recurring task with its frequency, effort and automation path (Jira rule, platform capability or AI agent).
  + Ship at least one automation per quarter that retires a recurring manual task, and report the hours returned.
  + Design and tune AI delivery agents for hygiene, summarisation and follow-up, with clear checks on their accuracy.
  + Contribute proven patterns to the DAO's Agentic Framework for cross-BL adoption.

* **Reporting and Delivery Insights**
  + Own the quantitative layer of executive reporting and recurring delivery briefs for your BLs, reconciled to source.
  + Draft the first qualitative read — what moved, why, and what's at risk — for your Senior Delivery Lead to sharpen.
  + Track the metrics the operating model is judged on: throughput, cycle time, WIP and goal coverage.

* **Tooling and Workflow Governance**
  + Own Jira configuration standards across your BLs: workflows, issue types, fields and boards.
  + Assess the impact of every workflow change request, align stakeholders on edge cases, and roll changes out without breaking reporting.

* **DAO-wide Ops Domain**
  + Own one operations domain for the whole DAO, such as release and change management, cadence design, or the reporting data layer.
  + Define the standard other Delivery Operations follow in that domain, and spot-check their output.

* **Enablement and Team Leverage**
  + Own the playbooks and onboarding that teach teams the Amplified Squads model and our tooling.
  + Review and coach the work of Delivery Operations peers.
  + Work against explicit Lead-readiness milestones agreed with your Senior Delivery Lead: run a BL review solo, lead a stakeholder alignment, own an escalation end to end with a recommendation.
  + Act as Delivery Lead backup for your BL during leave or peak load.

**Who You Are:**

* 4+ years in delivery operations, PMO, program coordination or Atlassian administration in a fast-moving technology company, including 1+ year owning operations for a team or BL rather than executing tasks.
* Expert in Jira: advanced JQL, dashboards, workflow and automation rules, and how field and screen configuration drive data quality.
* Proven automator: you have retired a manual process with Jira automation, scripts or AI, and can say how many hours it returned.
* Hands-on with AI tools (Claude, Cursor or equivalent) in operational workflows — demonstrated, not aspirational.
* Comfortable with data: you reconcile sources, spot anomalies, and read throughput, cycle time and aging.
* Influence without authority: EMs and PMs keep their work current because you made it easy, not because you chased them.
* You treat process debt the way engineers treat tech debt, and you write operating docs people actually follow.
* You want the path to Delivery Lead and can name your own gap to it.
* Scripting or SQL and BI tooling are a plus.
